headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channel or overlapping write surface is documented, but Airflow’s broad egress and the sample repo’s unknown runtime keep indirect misuse and compliance uncertainty non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between airflow and spring-integration-samples. Airflow has broad network egress, but spring-integration-samples exposes no input surface or bridge that would let attacker-controlled content flow into Airflow by default. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy outputs from one agent into the other without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows shared workspace, shared OAuth, or sensitive data classes. Airflow touches no declared data classes and spring-integration-samples also lists none, so there is no documented path for one agent to leak the other’s data by default.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same writable workspace, leakage risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid placing secrets in either agent’s working tree.
Review any shared mounts before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while spring-integration-samples has network egress none, so there is no documented overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource. Uncertainty remains because both are unverified source-based profiles, but the pairwise conflict pathway is not shown.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo.
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add file locks for shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can automate workflows, but spring-integration-samples is only documented as a sample repository with no action-taking authority. There is no evidence that B treats A’s output as authoritative, so cascading error is limited to manual misuse rather than a default automated chain.
conditions: IF outputs from airflow are fed into an automated workflow in spring-integration-samples without verification, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on outputs.
Add validation checks between agents.
Keep generated artifacts read-only until reviewed.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either airflow or spring-integration-samples. Because both profiles are docs-only and unverified, compliance risk is mostly uncertainty rather than a demonstrated violation; the other agent is not cited beyond confirming the pair lacks such metadata.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data under a residency or retention constraint, compliance risk becomes material.
mitigations: Document data residency for both agents.
Avoid regulated data until policies are confirmed.
Check retention settings before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
